title: Automated coronary calcification ratios track atherectomy classification
summary: Neural segmentation quantified coronary calcification and lumen volume in a 72-patient CT angiography study. Their ratio was associated with recorded rotational-atherectomy classifications. A threshold chosen from the same labeled cohort produced apparent accuracy of 0.75, so this is exploratory derivation-sample evidence. It does not establish independent diagnostic accuracy, replacement of invasive assessment or benefit from model-guided care.

source_review.scope: Primary model/clinical-application Methods and Results, exact primary article identity and current PubMed notices checked; derivation-only threshold and demographic reporting discrepancy retained.

evidence.tested: Patient-wise segmentation evaluation and exploratory comparison of automated volume ratios with clinical atherectomy classification in the derivation cohort.
evidence.unknown: Independent clinical threshold validation and patient benefit are unestablished; reported sex counts do not sum to the stated cohort total.
evidence.ai_role: A variational autoencoder and attention-based neural system delineate vessels and calcification for clinical volume-ratio analysis.
